sample_unit: non-IPF ILD subjects with CT scans under reference and non-reference imaging protocols

links.outcome: Model specificity under non-reference CT imaging protocols versus reference conditions
links.effect: Overall specificity decreased for all three DL models (p < 0.05 for two of three); mean effective mAs was a key factor for at least one model (p < 0.001).
links.quote: For all three DL models, the overall specificity of the previously trained IPF diagnosis model decreased (p < 0.05 for two out of three models).

links.outcome: Performance variation across CT acquisition and reconstruction protocols, scanner models
links.effect: Specificity dropped under non-reference imaging protocols; effective mAs and slice thickness (3 mm; p = 0.03) were significant factors for some models.
links.quote: Preliminary findings demonstrated the lack of robustness of IPF diagnosis model when the DL-based model is applied to CT series collected under different imaging protocols

screen.reason: Evaluates the robustness of existing deep learning models for IPF diagnosis across non-reference CT acquisition/reconstruction protocols (stress testing/external protocol shift), but does not test a specific deployment intervention or guardrail.
